value: fair use (training); not fair use (pirated library)
refers_to: Summary-judgment holding on training vs pirated copies
quote: To summarize the analysis that now follows, the use of the books at issue to train Claude and its precursors was exceedingly transformative and was a fair use under Section 107 of the Copyright Act. ... However, Anthropic had no entitlement to use pirated copies for its central library. Creating a permanent, general-purpose library was not itself a fair use excusing Anthropic’s piracy.
source_title: Bartz v. Anthropic PBC, No. C 24-05417 WHA, Order on Fair Use (Dkt. 231)
publisher: U.S. District Court, N.D. Cal. (Judge William Alsup)
notes: District-court ruling, not binding precedent; case settled before trial/appeal. Ellipsis omits sentence on print-to-digital scanning (also fair use).

refers_to: Pirated book copies downloaded (per SJ record)

source_title: Bartz v. Anthropic PBC, No. C 24-05417 WHA, Order on Fair Use (Dkt. 231)
publisher: U.S. District Court, N.D. Cal. (Judge William Alsup)
notes: On pirated copies the order 'accepted the Authors’ version of the facts' (summary-judgment posture). Settlement notice: ~40% of ~7M files were duplicates; ~4M unique works.

refers_to: Anthropic bought and destructively scanned print books
quote: Anthropic spent many millions of dollars to purchase millions of print books, often in used condition. Then, its service providers stripped the books from their bindings, cut their pages to size, and scanned the books into digital form
source_title: Bartz v. Anthropic PBC, No. C 24-05417 WHA, Order on Fair Use (Dkt. 231)
publisher: U.S. District Court, N.D. Cal. (Judge William Alsup)
notes: Court held this print-to-digital conversion was fair use.

refers_to: Kadrey v. Meta fair-use ruling scope

notes: Same order: 'This is not a class action, so the ruling only affects the rights of these thirteen authors'. Also: 'in most cases the answer will likely be yes' (that unpermitted training is illegal) — dicta.
